analysis.title: Genius Sports Ltd. (GENI) Q3'26 Review: Continued Execution Against Long-Term Secular Growth Opportunities (Prediction Markets + Legend)
key_insights: Goldman maintains Buy on GENI and cuts the 12-month price target to $9.00 from $10.50, citing lower forward estimates after the Q3'26 report and management's updated commentary. Price was $5.92 at the 5 Nov 2026 close, implying 52.0% upside.
Q3'26 revenue was $270m, 4% above GS ($260m) and 3% above consensus ($261m), up 62% YoY and 38% QoQ. Guidance was $260m.

Betting Content & Services revenue was $153m (+33% YoY), 10% above GS and 4% above consensus. Management cited a strong start to the NFL season, more in-play betting and pricing uplift on recent contract renewals.

Media Content & Sports Tech Services revenue was $117m (+127% YoY), 4% below GS ($122m) and 4% above consensus ($113m). Legend integration and new advertiser sign-ups in the quarter are cited as signs of long-term potential.

Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $87m vs GS $85m and consensus $86m (guidance $85m). Adj. EBITDA margin was 32.3% vs 32.6% GS and 32.8% consensus. Incremental adj. EBITDA margins improved sequentially and management points to continued margin expansion toward its FY28 targets.
GAAP gross profit was $92m vs GS $122m and consensus $110m. GAAP gross margin was 34.1% vs 46.8% GS and 42.1% consensus. GAAP EPS was $(0.06) vs GS $0.07 and consensus $(0.00).

Management positions prediction markets as a meaningful growth opportunity across customer acquisition, real-time data and settlement. GS expects investor focus on the pace and size of prediction market monetization.
GS flags elevated regulatory uncertainty around prediction markets because market structure is likely to evolve over the coming years.

The raised FY26 revenue guide implies limited incremental upside in Q4, because the raise largely reflects Q3 outperformance. Capitalized software development costs remain elevated and growing as a share of revenue.

Estimate changes: Q4'26 revenue $365m (from $376m), adj. EBITDA $129m (from $125m), GAAP EPS $0.07 (from $0.19). FY27 revenue $1.29bn (from $1.36bn), adj. EBITDA $394m (from $447m), GAAP EPS $0.04 (from $0.57).
The FY27 cut is concentrated in Media: FY27 Media revenue falls 17% to $528m from $633m, while FY27 Betting Content & Services rises 5% to $763m from $727m.
FY26 estimates: revenue $1,018m (guidance $1.015-1.035bn), adj. EBITDA $292m (guidance $287-297m), GAAP EPS $(0.47) vs $(0.23) before.

The price target blends 9.5x EV/GAAP EBITDA (unchanged) on NTM+1 estimates with 11.0x EV/(FCF-SBC) (from 13.5x) on NTM+4 estimates discounted back 3 years at 12%. The lower multiple reflects lower FCF-SBC estimates and uncertainty around forward FCF generation.
Scenario values are $4.00 downside (-32%), $9.00 base (+52%) and $11.50 upside (+94%).

GS expects structurally stronger FCF generation, supporting deleveraging. It projects FCF of $(87.0)m in 2026E, $78.2m in 2027E and $237.1m in 2028E. Net debt/EBITDA is projected at 1.8x in 2026E, 1.2x in 2027E and 0.4x in 2028E.

market_movers.rationale: Buy maintained and PT cut to $9.00 from $10.50 on lower FY27 forward estimates, mainly Media, and a lower EV/(FCF-SBC) multiple. Prediction markets and Legend are cited as long-term growth drivers.

trade_ideas.description: Buy GENI shares with a 12-month price target of $9.00
trade_ideas.rationale: Secular growth in online sports betting, in-play betting, prediction markets and Media, plus improving operating leverage and FCF.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower online gaming growth, regulatory uncertainty around prediction markets, higher data rights cost inflation, loss of exclusive data rights, and higher corporate costs without matching revenue.

risk_factors: Slower growth of online gaming from more gradual consumer adoption or less favorable legislation.
Slower penetration of customer wallets from lower adoption of GENI's products.
Higher rights cost inflation than modeled, driven by leagues and/or direct competitors.
Loss of exclusivity on key data rights, or loss of rights at renewal to competitors.
Greater corporate cost investment without commensurate revenue benefits.
Regulatory uncertainty around prediction markets remains elevated as market structure evolves.
Capitalized software development costs remain elevated and growing as a share of revenue.
The Q4 guide implies limited incremental upside because the FY26 raise largely reflects Q3 outperformance.
